prompt:
Refine the FIRST attached website design, Reflected Light, for Missional by Design. One continuous production-quality homepage mock, 1440px wide and 2400px tall, no browser chrome. Keep its recognizable editorial rhythm, confident Instrument Serif headings and Mona Sans readable body, dark navy ink, luminous pale icy blue and white. This is a refinement of the selected direction, not a new concept.

Reference 2 is the APPROVED rock specimen: preserve its exact broad fractured rocky outline, blue-silver mirror faces and sharp four-point reflected glint; use this specimen rather than inventing a smoother crystal or dented rock. Reference 3 is the approved fictional startup/urban workshop photograph. Preserve its rich warm colour, real working scene and subtle analog feeling. No biblical props, literal cross cutouts or new abstract stone icons.

Improve first reference:
1. Much less blue haze. Mostly clean white/very pale blue surfaces, restrained light and localized glow; no cloudy smoke. Hero is spatial and generous with one large rock right and heading left. Large strong serif headline “What really is good news here?” Deck “Christian reflection and practical tools for a changing context.” Primary action “Find your starting point”. Small readable line “An open resource for Christian technologists and ministry leaders.” No decorative microtype slogans.
2. Navigation Principles, Canvas, Patterns, Writing, About, EN / DE. Stacked serif missional / — by — / design wordmark.
3. Early human photo: large edge-to-edge warm workshop image, with NO headline/body overlay on faces or busy photo. Put heading and short paragraph on an adjacent clean white editorial strip: “Faithful design starts with listening.” Text “To people. To our changing context. To the good news of Jesus.” Small caption “Generated editorial image”. Do not claim we are a community or global movement. This is an open resource by Tobias Treppmann.
4. Retain the strong applied example “A missed day. A welcoming return.” One short sentence “How might a reading app help someone begin again?” A clearly labelled “Illustrative design options” shows two simple welcoming return screens; no shame, performance metrics, real app names, or invented observed evidence. Link “Compare the options”. No handwritten annotations or decorative arrows.
5. Three elegant resource columns, simple line icons from a coherent established icon family, generous whitespace rather than cards. “Principles” — “Connect Christian purpose with everyday design decisions.” “Canvas” — “Explore what good news means in your context.” “Patterns” — “Compare design options for Bible and faith products.” Links “Explore principles”, “Open the canvas”, “Browse patterns”.
6. REMOVE the unrelated mountain image completely. A calm closing editorial section uses the actual neighborhood scene from reference 2 as an intentional wide photograph, with heading OUTSIDE the photo: “Our context keeps changing.” Short copy “Faithful responses begin with renewed attention.” Link “Explore the perspective”. Caption “Generated neighborhood vignette”. Compact footer “An open resource by Tobias Treppmann.”
No invented endorsements, publications, membership claims, documentary captions or testimonials. No large black slabs. Preserve generous whitespace, varying scale and strong editorial flow. No more than two type families; body equivalent 18–20px at desktop, reading measure under65 characters. Crisp semantic-looking readable text, no repeated content just to fill space. Date16October2026; no visible dates needed. This mock should show the luminous identity with warmth and specificity, not a generic SaaS landing page.
